mainTopic: An אשם compared to a חטאת: לשמה, blood above the red line, and blood brought inside
overview: This amud continues the debate between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע about an אשם slaughtered שלא לשמה. רבי אליעזר first learns it from the word "הוא", which appears by חטאת and פסח. רבי יהושע answers that by אשם the word "הוא" is said about the burning of the אימורין, and that step does not hold the קרבן back. רבי אליעזר then brings the פסוק "כחטאת כאשם". The גמרא asks why רבי יהושע pointed only to the difference that a חטאת's blood goes above the red line, when other differences seem available. It answers each one and concludes that he simply picked one of several reasons. The גמרא then asks why רבי אליעזר did not say an אשם's blood also goes above. After several logical proofs are tried and knocked down, the answer is that the word "אותה" limits blood-above to the חטאת. Finally, the גמרא quotes a משנה about blood brought into the היכל and asks for the reason of the חכמים. רבא begins a קל וחומר from the עולה, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The argument is going in circles
steps.stepSummary: The previous round of the debate closes. The speaker says he is going back to his earlier point, so the arguments are circling around.
steps.simpleTranslation: I come back to my earlier point; we are going around in circles.
steps.whatsHappening: The last round of the debate ends here. The speaker says the arguments have looped back to where they started.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line refers back to the earlier distinction: a חטאת is unique because its blood is put on the upper part of the מזבח, so it cannot be compared to an אשם. By saying "I return," the speaker shows that the earlier comparisons did not overcome that distinction. This is what pushes רבי אליעזר to try a completely new type of proof in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: I go back (to my earlier point)
around in a circle

phrases.english: I return around in a circle.
phrases.notes: He means: I go back to my earlier point that a חטאת is different because its blood goes on the top part of the מזבח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the earlier back-and-forth of comparisons between חטאת and אשם.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole previous line of comparisons from חטאת to אשם.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Every comparison runs back into the same distinction: חטאת is unique because its blood goes on the upper part of the מזבח.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's new source: "הוא" by חטאת and פסח
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר starts a new proof. By חטאת and by פסח the תורה says "הוא" about slaughtering, and this teaches that only slaughter לשמה is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר came back with another argument. By a חטאת the תורה says "it" about slaughtering: if it is slaughtered for its own sake it is fit, and if not for its own sake it is unfit. By a פסח the תורה says "it" about slaughtering: for its sake it is fit, not for its sake it is unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר is setting up his new proof. He first shows two cases where the word "הוא" teaches that wrong intent makes the קרבן פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the debate was about whether אשם is similar to חטאת in its features. Now רבי אליעזר switches to a word-based source. In both models, חטאת and פסח, the word "הוא" appears in connection with slaughtering, and it is read as "only this way": only לשמה, or the קרבן is פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: he argued it with a different line of reasoning
for its own sake (with the correct intent for this קרבן)
not for its own sake (with the wrong intent)
slaughtering a זבח

phrases.aramaic: חָזַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וְדָנוֹ דִּין אַחֵר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer went back and argued it with a different argument:
A sin offering: "it" is stated about it in connection with slaughter –
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:24

phrases.english: "it": for its sake, it is fit;
not for its sake, it is unfit.
And a Paschal offering: "it" is stated about it in connection with slaughter –
phrases.notes: שמות 12:27

phrases.english: "it": for its sake, it is fit;
not for its sake, it is unfit.

steps.triggerLanguage: חָזַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וְדָנוֹ דִּין אַחֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the earlier comparisons stalled, רבי אליעזר starts a fresh proof based on the wording of the פסוקים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word "הוא" by the slaughter of חטאת and פסח teaches that slaughter שלא לשמה makes them פסול.

steps.title: Applying "הוא" to the אשם
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר finishes his proof. The פסוק of אשם also says "הוא", so an אשם שלא לשמה should also be פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: The word "it" is also said about an אשם. So here too: for its sake it is fit, not for its sake it is unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר brings his proof home. Since the אשם also has the word "הוא", it should follow the same rule as חטאת and פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is simple: same word, same rule. If "הוא" means "only לשמה" by חטאת and פסח, it should mean the same by אשם. That would make an אשם שלא לשמה פסול, which is exactly רבי אליעזר's position.

keyTerms.meaning: also, likewise
guilt offering

phrases.english: So too a guilt offering: "it" is stated about it –
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:5

phrases.english: "it": for its sake, it is fit;
not for its sake, it is unfit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the rule built in step 2 to the case being debated, the אשם.
steps.raayaObject: That an אשם slaughtered שלא לשמה is פסול.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The word "הוא" in the פסוק of אשם, matching the "הוא" by חטאת and פסח.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: the "הוא" of אשם is said about something that does not hold it back
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע accepts the rule for חטאת and פסח. But he points out that by אשם the word "הוא" comes after the burning of the אימורין. An אשם is כשר even if the אימורין were never burned, so this "הוא" cannot make it פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said to him: By a חטאת "it" is said about slaughtering, so for its sake it is fit and not for its sake it is unfit. By a פסח "it" is said about slaughtering, so for its sake it is fit and not for its sake it is unfit. But by an אשם, "it" is said only after the burning of the אימורין. And the אשם itself, even if its אימורין were not burned at all, is fit!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע rejects the proof. The "הוא" by אשם is not about slaughtering. It is about the burning of the אימורין, and that burning is not even required for the אשם to be כשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע agrees that "הוא" can teach "only לשמה," but only when it is attached to a step that matters for whether the קרבן is כשר. By חטאת and פסח it is attached to the slaughtering, which is essential. By אשם it is attached to the burning of the אימורין. If the אימורין are not burned at all, the אשם is still כשר, so burning them with the wrong intent surely cannot make it פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: burning the fats and parts of the קרבן that go on the מזבח
the parts of a קרבן that are burned on the מזבח
itself
fit, valid

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר learns from the word "הוא" that an אשם שלא לשמה is פסול, like חטאת and פסח. רבי יהושע answers that by אשם the "הוא" is said about the burning of the אימורין, which does not hold back the קרבן. So it cannot teach that the אשם becomes פסול.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהושע is not saying the word "הוא" never teaches anything. He agrees it works for חטאת and פסח. His point is about where the word is placed: by אשם it is attached to a step that does not affect whether the קרבן is כשר.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key principle in this sugya. A word like "הוא" only makes a קרבן פסול if it is attached to an essential part of the עבודה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him:
A sin offering: "it" is stated about it in connection with slaughter –
"it": for its sake, it is fit;
not for its sake, it is unfit.
A Paschal offering: "it" is stated about it in connection with slaughter –
"it": for its sake, it is fit;
not for its sake, it is unfit.
But a guilt offering: "it" is not stated about it –
except after the burning of the sacrificial portions,
phrases.notes: In ויקרא 7:5 the words "it is an אשם" come right after the פסוק describes burning the parts on the מזבח.

phrases.aramaic: וְהוּא עַצְמוֹ שֶׁלֹּא הוּקְטְרוּ אֵימוּרִין – כָּשֵׁר!
phrases.english: and it itself, where the sacrificial portions were not burned – is fit!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly rejects רבי אליעזר's proof from the word "הוא" in step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the application of "הוא" to אשם. The rule for חטאת and פסח is accepted.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: By אשם the word "הוא" is attached to the burning of the אימורין, not to slaughtering, and that burning does not hold back the כשרות of the קרבן.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר proves from a comparison פסוק that an אשם שלא לשמה is פסול
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר brings the פסוק ״כחטאת כאשם״. The תורה puts אשם side by side with חטאת, so an אשם שלא לשמה is פסול just like a חטאת שלא לשמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר said to him: The פסוק says, "As is the sin offering, so is the guilt offering." Just as a sin offering not for its sake is invalid, a guilt offering not for its sake is also invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע knocked down the proof from the word ״הוא״. So רבי אליעזר brings a different proof: a פסוק that directly compares אשם to חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This proof does not depend on where the word ״הוא״ appears in the פסוק. The תורה itself says אשם is like חטאת. Since a חטאת שלא לשמה is פסול, the comparison carries the same rule over to אשם.

keyTerms.meaning: "As is the sin offering, so is the guilt offering" (the פסוק that compares the two)
Not for its own sake, meaning slaughtered with the wrong offering in mind
"Just as ... so too": the pattern for carrying a rule from one case to another
Invalid; the קרבן does not count

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said to him:
Behold, it says:
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is the corrected wording. Read it as "the פסוק says."

phrases.english: "As is the sin offering, so is the guilt offering"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:7

phrases.english: just as a sin offering not for its sake is invalid,
so too a guilt offering not for its sake is invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, הֲרֵי הוּא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבי יהושע rejected the proof from ״הוא״, רבי אליעזר switches to a new source: the comparison of אשם to חטאת.
steps.raayaObject: An אשם שלא לשמה is פסול.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק ״כחטאת כאשם״ (ויקרא 7:7), which compares אשם to חטאת.

steps.title: Why not combine the חטאת and the פסח into one proof?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהושע's words ״חוזרני חלילה״ from the ברייתא. Then it asks: why didn't רבי אליעזר go back and prove his point with a מה הצד, using what חטאת and פסח have in common?
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: רבי יהושע said to him, "I go back around in a circle." The גמרא asks: Let the argument go back to the start, and let him prove it from the common element of the two sources!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops quoting the ברייתא and starts discussing it. It asks why רבי אליעזר did not use a stronger kind of proof that combines two sources.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each source alone could be pushed away. חטאת has its own special feature, and so does פסח. But when you put חטאת and פסח together, maybe no single special feature is left to push the proof away. Then you could learn from what they share that אשם שלא לשמה is also פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: "I go back around": the argument is going in circles
Let the argument go back to its starting point
A proof built from the common element of two sources

phrases.english: The Master said:
phrases.notes: The ברייתא is finished. Now the גמרא goes back and picks apart one of its lines.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him:
I go back around in a circle.
But let the argument go back around,
and let him derive it with "the common element"!
phrases.notes: He means: take חטאת and פסח together and learn אשם from what the two share.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The ברייתא is done. The גמרא now asks about the circular argument mentioned there and suggests a better proof רבי אליעזר could have used.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's choice to switch to a new proof, instead of bringing the argument back around with a מה הצד from חטאת and פסח, once רבי יהושע said the debate was going in circles.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A מה הצד from חטאת and פסח together should get past the differences of each one alone, so it should have worked.

steps.title: The combined proof fails because both share the element of כרת
steps.stepSummary: The מה הצד does not work. חטאת and פסח both have a connection to כרת, and אשם does not. So their common element is itself something special that אשם lacks.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because one can refute it: What about the common element of the two? They both have an element of כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. The combined proof can be pushed away because חטאת and פסח share a strict feature that אשם does not have.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מה הצד only works if the common element is not something special. Here, both sources are tied to כרת. A חטאת comes for a sin that carries כרת, and someone who does not bring a פסח gets כרת. Since אשם has no such link, maybe the rule of לשמה only applies to קרבנות connected to כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: To refute or knock down a proof
The common element shared by the two sources
Spiritual cutting off, a severe punishment from Heaven

phrases.english: Because one can refute it:
What about the common element shared by them?
They have an element of karet.
phrases.notes: A חטאת comes for a sin punished with כרת, and skipping the פסח brings כרת. An אשם has neither.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6 by showing that the מה הצד can be refuted.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Pointing out a shared strictness (פירכא) that both sources have and the target case lacks.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Combining חטאת and פסח would prove that אשם שלא לשמה is פסול.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both sources share כרת, which אשם lacks, so the combined proof fails. That is why רבי אליעזר needed a different source.
steps.whatToRemember: A מה הצד proof fails if the two sources share a strict feature that the new case lacks. Here that feature is כרת.

steps.title: Why didn't רבי יהושע use a stronger difference about the חטאת's blood?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהושע's refutation: a חטאת is different because its blood goes above the red line. Then it asks why he didn't give a stronger difference: חטאת blood can even enter לפני ולפנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said to him: No. If you said this about a sin offering, that is because its blood is placed above. The גמרא asks: Let him say instead: No. If you said this about a sin offering, that is because its blood enters the innermost place!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another line of the ברייתא, where רבי יהושע shows that חטאת is different from אשם. It then asks why he picked that difference and not a bigger one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע said: you can't learn אשם from חטאת, because חטאת blood goes on the upper part of the מזבח. The גמרא asks why he didn't mention a much more striking difference: some חטאת blood is even brought into the innermost holy place, which never happens with אשם. The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: Above, meaning the blood is placed on the upper half of the מזבח
"Let him say to him": why not give this answer instead?
The innermost place, the קודש הקדשים

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him: No;
if you said so about a sin offering,
that is because its blood is placed above!
phrases.notes: Above the red line around the middle of the מזבח. An אשם's blood goes below it.

phrases.english: But let him say to him: No;
if you said so about a sin offering,
that is because its blood enters the innermost place!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֵימָא לֵיהּ: לֹא; אִם אָמַרְתָּ בְּחַטָּאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא moves on from the circular-argument question to another line of the ברייתא: רבי יהושע's refutation of learning אשם from חטאת.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע's choice of the difference ״דמה למעלה״.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is a stronger difference available (חטאת blood entering לפני ולפנים), so why did he use the weaker one?
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two differences. ״דמה למעלה״ is about where the blood goes on the outer מזבח. ״לפני ולפנים״ is about blood brought all the way inside to the קודש הקדשים.

steps.title: The comparison is only to the חטאות החיצוניות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי אליעזר compares אשם only to the חטאות החיצוניות, whose blood never goes into the לפני ולפנים. So רבי יהושע could not point to that difference.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are talking about the outer sin offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 8. רבי יהושע could not say "חטאת blood goes into the לפני ולפנים," because the comparison is only to the outer חטאות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some חטאות have their blood brought inside, and some have it put on the outer מזבח. רבי אליעזר's comparison of אשם to חטאת is to the outer kind, and their blood never enters the לפני ולפנים. So that difference does not apply here, while 'above the red line' does apply to outer חטאות.

keyTerms.meaning: The outer sin offerings, whose blood is put on the outer מזבח
The inner sin offerings, whose blood is brought inside
We are saying / we are talking about

phrases.english: We are speaking about the outer sin offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 8
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the comparison is limited to the outer חטאות
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהושע should have said that חטאת blood can go into the לפני ולפנים
steps.terutzMaskana: The comparison is only to the outer חטאות, which never go inside, so that difference does not apply

steps.title: An outer חטאת is פסול if its blood goes inside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back. Even with the outer חטאות, there is a difference: if their blood is brought into the לפני ולפנים, the חטאת becomes פסול. Why didn't רבי יהושע use that?
steps.simpleTranslation: [He should have said:] that if its blood went into the innermost holy place, it is disqualified!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges again. רבי יהושע could have said that an outer חטאת becomes פסול if its blood is brought inside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 limited the comparison to outer חטאות. But that limit itself gives a new difference: an outer חטאת whose blood was wrongly taken inside is פסול. If an אשם does not share that rule, it is a clear way to separate the two.

keyTerms.meaning: The innermost holy place, the קודש הקדשים
Its blood entered
Disqualified

phrases.english: That if its blood entered
phrases.notes: Read this as what רבי יהושע could have said: 'A חטאת is different, since if its blood entered...'

phrases.english: into the innermost sanctum, it is disqualified!
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is the corrected wording.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁאִם נִכְנַס דָּמָהּ לִפְנַי וְלִפְנִים פְּסוּלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of Step 9 by finding a new difference inside the outer-חטאת case
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יהושע had no better difference once we talk about outer חטאות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An outer חטאת whose blood was brought inside is פסול. That is a difference from אשם that רבי יהושע could have used.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר holds an אשם is the same
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי אליעזר holds that an אשם whose blood was brought inside is also פסול. So this is not a difference at all according to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר holds: "also the guilt offering."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. According to רבי אליעזר, this rule applies to an אשם too, so רבי יהושע could not use it against him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A difference only works if both sides agree it is a difference. רבי אליעזר holds that an אשם whose blood went inside is also פסול. So for him, חטאת and אשם are the same here, and the point would not refute him.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds / he has the view
Also the guilt offering (the same rule applies to it)
Guilt offering

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer holds
"also the guilt offering."
phrases.notes: He means an אשם whose blood was brought inside is also פסול, just like a חטאת.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אַף הָאָשָׁם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: The proposed difference does not exist according to רבי אליעזר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only a חטאת becomes פסול if its blood goes inside, so this is a difference
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אליעזר holds an אשם is also פסול in that case, so it is no difference for him

steps.title: A חטאת atones for sins that carry כרת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks again: רבי יהושע could have said that a חטאת is different because it atones for sins that carry כרת, which an אשם does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: [He should have said:] that it atones for those who are liable to כרת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises one more difference that רבי יהושע could have used. A חטאת atones for sins whose punishment for doing them on purpose is כרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the 'inside' difference was answered, the גמרא looks for another one. A חטאת comes for sins that carry כרת, and an אשם does not. That seems like a strong reason to treat חטאת as special, and the question is why רבי יהושע did not say it.

keyTerms.meaning: Atones
Those liable to כרת (sins punished by כרת when done on purpose)
Since / for it is so that

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the same point as Step 7. There, כרת was used to reject a מה הצד from חטאת and פסח together. Here, the גמרא suggests it as a direct difference רבי יהושע could have given between חטאת and אשם.

phrases.english: Since it atones for those liable to karet!
phrases.notes: Again, read this as what רבי יהושע could have said about a חטאת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 11 removed the 'inside' difference, this raises a new difference
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that רבי יהושע chose the best available difference between חטאת and אשם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A חטאת atones for sins that carry כרת, and an אשם does not. This is an obvious difference, so why did רבי יהושע not use it?

steps.title: רבי אליעזר compares only to the חטאת of שמיעת הקול
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי אליעזר learns from the חטאת of שמיעת הקול. That sin does not carry כרת, so the כרת difference does not apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from the חטאת of שמיעת הקול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 12. רבי אליעזר compares the אשם to a specific kind of חטאת that does not come for a כרת sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 12 the גמרא asked why רבי יהושע did not say that a חטאת atones for כרת sins. The answer is that רבי אליעזר's comparison uses the חטאת of שמיעת הקול, a sin with no כרת. So against that חטאת, the כרת difference does not exist.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'hearing the voice.' Someone hears a call to testify and falsely swears he knows nothing.
The oath of testimony, which is the sin behind שמיעת הקול.
Being 'cut off,' a heavenly punishment. Most sins that need a חטאת carry it.

phrases.english: From the sin offering of 'hearing the voice.'
phrases.notes: This is the person who falsely swore he had no testimony (ויקרא 5:1). That sin does not carry כרת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the כרת challenge of Step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: it identifies which חטאת the comparison uses.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed רבי אליעזר compared אשם to חטאות in general, and most of those come for כרת sins.
steps.terutzMaskana: The comparison is to the חטאת of שמיעת הקול, which has no כרת, so that difference falls away.

steps.title: But a חטאת needs four placements of blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests another difference that רבי יהושע could have used: a חטאת needs four placements of blood, and an אשם does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a חטאת is different, because it needs four placements of blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes another difference between חטאת and אשם that רבי יהושע could have pointed to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even the חטאת of שמיעת הקול needs its blood placed four times on the מזבח. An אשם usually gets only two placements. If that is a real difference, רבי יהושע could have used it to break רבי אליעזר's comparison.

keyTerms.meaning: Placements of blood on the מזבח.
It requires.
'Since it' or 'because it.' This word introduces a difference that can break a comparison.

phrases.english: But it requires four placements!
phrases.notes: 'It' is the חטאת. The point is that an אשם usually gets only two placements.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the answer of Step 13 and then raises a new difference.
steps.kashyaTarget: The question of why רבי יהושע picked a weaker difference.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even the חטאת of שמיעת הקול differs from an אשם in how many blood placements it needs. So רבי יהושע had a ready difference to use.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר may hold like רבי ישמעאל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי אליעזר may agree with רבי ישמעאל, who says all blood needs four placements. Then the number of placements is not a difference.
steps.simpleTranslation: He may hold like רבי ישמעאל, who says all blood needs four placements.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 14 by suggesting that רבי אליעזר follows רבי ישמעאל's view about blood placements.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי ישמעאל, all blood gets four placements, including the blood of an אשם. If רבי אליעזר agrees, a חטאת and an אשם are the same in this detail. That is why רבי יהושע could not use it against him.

keyTerms.meaning: All the blood, meaning the blood of every offering.

phrases.english: In accordance with Rabbi Yishmael, who says:
All the blood requires four placements.
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets. The word in square brackets is the corrected wording, plural to match 'all the blood.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the four-placements challenge of Step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Linking רבי אליעזר to another תנא's view, so the supposed difference disappears.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only a חטאת needs four placements, and an אשם needs two.
steps.terutzMaskana: Following רבי ישמעאל, every offering, including an אשם, needs four placements. So there is no difference.

steps.title: But a חטאת's blood must go on all four corners
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests one more difference: a חטאת's blood must be placed on all four corners of the מזבח. Step 17 answers this.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a חטאת is different, because its blood must go on the four corners.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes yet another difference that רבי יהושע could have used. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the number of placements is the same, the place of the placements may differ. A חטאת's blood goes onto the four horns, the corners, of the מזבח. An אשם's blood is not placed that way. So the גמרא asks again why רבי יהושע did not point to this.

keyTerms.meaning: The horns, the raised corners of the מזבח.
All four corners of the מזבח.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'four placements' (Step 14) with 'four corners' (this step). Step 14 asked how many times the blood is placed. This step asks where it is placed: on the horns at all four corners.

phrases.english: But it requires placement on four horns!
phrases.notes: The 'horns' are the raised corners of the מזבח. A חטאת's blood goes on all of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the רבי ישמעאל answer about the number of placements, then points to a difference in where the blood is placed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The question of why רבי יהושע picked a weaker difference.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even if the number of placements matches, a חטאת's blood goes on the four horns and an אשם's does not. That is a clear difference רבי יהושע could have raised.

steps.title: רבי יהושע just picked one of several reasons
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that there are many differences between a חטאת and an אשם (finger, corner, edge of the corner), and רבי יהושע simply mentioned one of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And by your logic, there is also the finger, the corner, and the edge of the corner! Rather, he mentioned one of two or three reasons.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops asking 'why didn't רבי יהושע use this other difference?' It answers that he had several good reasons available and only needed to say one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חטאת has many special rules that an אשם does not have: the blood is placed with the כהן's finger, on the corner of the מזבח, or on the very edge of the corner. Nobody would expect רבי יהושע to list every one of them. So the fact that he named only one difference does not mean he rejected the others.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning: turning the questioner's logic back on him
Finger: a חטאת's blood is placed with the כהן's finger
Corner (literally 'horn') of the מזבח
Its edge: the very tip of the corner
Reasons or arguments

steps.whatToRemember: When a תנא gives one reason, that does not mean it was his only reason. Here רבי יהושע had several differences to choose from and named just one.
steps.confusionAlert: This answer does not say the earlier challenges (כרת, four placements, four corners) were wrong. It says רבי יהושע did not have to mention every difference, so there is no question on him.

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning,
isn't there the finger!
phrases.notes: A חטאת's blood is put on the מזבח with the כהן's finger. Other offerings don't need that.

phrases.english: Isn't there the corner!
Isn't there its edge!
phrases.notes: The very tip of the מזבח's corner.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא חַד מִתְּרֵי תְּלָת טַעְמֵי נָקֵט.
phrases.english: Rather, he mentioned one of two or three reasons.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the still-open challenge of step 16, and closes the whole series of 'why didn't רבי יהושע say this difference' challenges.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Turning the question back: there are too many differences to list, so mentioning just one is enough.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבי יהושע named only one difference, he must not have accepted the other possible differences.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהושע had several valid differences and simply picked one of them.

steps.title: Why didn't רבי אליעזר say an אשם's blood also goes above?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהושע's rejection ('no, if you said') and asks why רבי אליעזר did not answer that an אשם's blood also goes above the red line.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: רבי יהושע said to him: No, if you said... Let רבי אליעזר say to him: an אשם's blood is also placed above!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a line in the ברייתא where רבי יהושע pointed out that a חטאת's blood goes above the red line and an אשם's goes below. It asks why רבי אליעזר did not just say an אשם's blood goes above too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר compares an אשם to a חטאת in its laws. If so, he could have said the אשם also has its blood placed above the red line around the מזבח (חוּט הַסִּיקְרָא). Then רבי יהושע's difference would disappear.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him say to him: why didn't he answer this way?
Above: the upper half of the מזבח, above the red line
Also

phrases.english: The Master said,
Rabbi Yehoshua said to him:
No, if you said...
phrases.notes: This points to the line in the ברייתא: you said it about a חטאת, whose blood goes above, but an אשם's blood goes below.

phrases.english: Let Rabbi Eliezer say to him:
A guilt offering's blood is also placed above!
phrases.notes: 'Above' means above the red line that runs around the middle of the מזבח.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא לֵיהּ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר: אָשָׁם נָמֵי דָּמוֹ לְמַעְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the many possible differences to the one difference רבי יהושע actually gave, and asks why רבי אליעזר did not reject it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's silence in the face of רבי יהושע's 'above versus below' difference.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since רבי אליעזר treats an אשם like a חטאת, he could have said the אשם's blood also goes above, which would cancel רבי יהושע's difference.

steps.title: אביי: a קל וחומר from an עולה shows an אשם's blood goes below
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that רבי אליעזר could not say that, because of a קל וחומר: an עולה is fully burned and still has its blood below, so an אשם, which is not fully burned, surely has its blood below.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: You cannot say an אשם's blood goes above, because of a קל וחומר from an עולה. If an עולה, which is entirely burned, has its blood placed below, then an אשם, which is not entirely burned, surely does too!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי explains why רבי אליעזר could not claim an אשם's blood goes above. A קל וחומר from an עולה would prove it goes below.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עולה is in one way more serious: the whole animal is burned on the מזבח (כָּלִיל). Even so, its blood goes below the red line. An אשם is not fully burned, so it is 'lighter', and if the heavier one goes below, the lighter one surely goes below as well.

keyTerms.meaning: You cannot say
An argument from a lighter case to a heavier one (or the reverse)
Entirely burned on the מזבח
Below: the lower half of the מזבח, below the red line
All the more so

phrases.english: Abaye said:
That a guilt offering's blood goes above
you cannot say,
because of an a fortiori argument from a burnt offering;
just as a burnt offering, which is entirely burned,
has its blood placed below,
a guilt offering, which is not entirely burned,
is it not all the more so?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: אָשָׁם דָּמוֹ לְמַעְלָה לָא מָצֵית אָמְרַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 18 by showing that רבי אליעזר could not claim an אשם's blood goes above.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A קל וחומר proving the opposite of the suggested claim.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אליעזר could simply say an אשם's blood goes above, like a חטאת.
steps.terutzMaskana: A קל וחומר from an עולה forces the אשם's blood to go below, so רבי אליעזר could not say that.

steps.title: The קל וחומר fails: an עולה does not atone
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects אביי's קל וחומר: an עולה is different because it does not atone, while an אשם does.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about an עולה? It is different, since it does not atone!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on אביי's proof. An עולה is 'lighter' in a different way: it does not atone, so it cannot prove anything about an אשם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר only works if the first case is more serious in every way that matters. An אשם atones and an עולה does not, so maybe atoning is exactly what earns the blood a place above the red line, like a חטאת. That breaks אביי's קל וחומר, and the question of step 18 comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: What about...? It is different, since...: the standard way to knock down a קל וחומר
Atones for a sin

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic way to break a קל וחומר: find one area where the 'heavier' case is actually lighter. That sends the גמרא back to looking for why רבי אליעזר did not use the 'above' answer.

phrases.english: What about a burnt offering?
It is different, since it does not atone!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אביי's קל וחומר from step 19.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only אביי's קל וחומר is rejected; the question of step 18 is open again.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: An עולה is not more serious in every way. It does not atone, so it cannot teach about an אשם, which does atone.

steps.title: The bird חטאת proves the point
steps.stepSummary: Against the claim that only a non-atoning offering has its blood below, the גמרא points to the bird חטאת, which does atone and still has its blood below.
steps.simpleTranslation: A bird sin offering proves it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the rejection from step 20 by bringing a different offering: the bird חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 said an עולה is different because it does not atone. A bird חטאת does atone for a sin, yet its blood is placed below the red line. So atoning does not force the blood to go above, and the אשם can still have its blood below.

keyTerms.meaning: A bird brought as a sin offering
Will prove (it shows the point is true)

phrases.english: A bird sin offering will prove it.
phrases.notes: A bird חטאת atones for a sin, and still its blood goes below the red line.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the rejection in step 20 by offering a new example that does atone.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Counter-example: an atoning offering whose blood is still below.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Atoning offerings have their blood above, so the אשם might too.
steps.terutzMaskana: The bird חטאת atones and has blood below, so atonement is not the deciding factor.

steps.title: The bird חטאת is not a slaughtered offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the bird חטאת proof: a bird חטאת is not slaughtered, so maybe that is why its blood goes below.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about a bird sin offering? It is special, because it is not a type of slaughtered offering!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof from the bird חטאת by pointing out how it is different from an אשם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bird חטאת is killed by מליקה (pinching the neck), not by שחיטה. Maybe its blood goes below only because it is not a regular slaughtered זבח. An אשם is slaughtered, so the bird proves nothing about it.

keyTerms.meaning: "What about...?" A formula that points out a weakness in a comparison
Since it is (introduces the special feature)
A type of slaughtered offering

phrases.english: What about a bird sin offering?
It is special, since it is not a type of slaughtered offering!

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְחַטַּאת הָעוֹף, שֶׁכֵּן אֵינָהּ מִין זֶבַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from step 21.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the bird חטאת.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The bird חטאת is not slaughtered, unlike an אשם, so its blood rule may come from that difference.

steps.title: Combining the עולה and the bird חטאת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings back the עולה and joins it with the bird חטאת: each one's weakness is covered by the other, and what they share (קדשי קדשים, blood below) applies to the אשם too.
steps.simpleTranslation: An עולה will prove it. This one is not like that one, and that one is not like this one. What they have in common is that they are קדשי קדשים and their blood goes below. So I will also include an אשם, which is קדשי קדשים, so its blood goes below.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the rejection by building a הצד השוה argument from two offerings together, the עולה and the bird חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The עולה is slaughtered, so the problem with the bird חטאת does not apply to it. The bird חטאת atones, so the problem with the עולה (step 20) does not apply to it. What is left in common is that both are קדשי קדשים with blood below, and the אשם is also קדשי קדשים, so its blood goes below too.

keyTerms.meaning: This one is not like that one: each case has its own feature
The feature they share
Offerings of the highest level of holiness
Below the red line on the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא forgot that the עולה was already rejected in step 20. Alone it was rejected, but together with the bird חטאת each one's weak point is covered by the other.
steps.whatToRemember: A הצד השוה works by taking two sources that each have a different weakness, and learning only from what they share.

phrases.english: A burnt offering will prove it.
phrases.notes: The עולה is slaughtered, so the bird's weakness does not apply to it.

phrases.english: The feature of this one is not like the feature of that one,
and the feature of that one is not like the feature of this one.
The feature they share is
that they are offerings of the highest holiness, and their blood goes below;
so I too will bring in a guilt offering,
which is of the highest holiness, so its blood goes below.

steps.triggerLanguage: עוֹלָה תּוֹכִיחַ. לֹא רְאִי זֶה כִּרְאִי זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the rejection in step 22 by combining the עולה with the bird חטאת.
steps.terutzResolutionType: הצד השוה: combining two sources so each covers the other's weakness.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each source alone has a weakness, so no proof about the אשם exists.
steps.terutzMaskana: Together, their shared feature (קדשי קדשים, blood below) teaches that an אשם's blood goes below.
steps.whyThisMatters: This argument supports אביי's claim (step 19) that רבי אליעזר could not say an אשם's blood goes above.

steps.title: רבא מפרזקיא: the אשם has a fixed price
steps.stepSummary: רבא מפרזקיא asks רב אשי why רבי אליעזר could not break the הצד השוה: the עולה and bird חטאת have no fixed value, but the אשם does.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא of Parzakya said to רב אשי: Let him refute it! What about the shared feature of those two? They have no fixed value. Can you say the same about an אשם, which has a fixed value?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא מפרזקיא challenges the הצד השוה argument from step 23 by finding a feature both sources share that the אשם does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A הצד השוה falls apart if the two sources share something the new case lacks. Neither the עולה nor the bird חטאת has a required minimum price, but an אשם must be worth a fixed amount. Maybe that is why their blood goes below, so רבי אליעזר could have broken the proof and said the אשם's blood goes above.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him refute it (point out a difference that breaks the proof)
A fixed set amount (here, a required minimum value)
Can you say? (questions whether the comparison holds)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא מִפַּרְזִקְיָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rava of Parzakya said to Rav Ashi:
But let him refute it:
phrases.notes: "Him" is רבי אליעזר, who could have broken this proof.

phrases.english: What about the shared feature of them?
They are special, since they have no fixed value;
can you say the same about a guilt offering, which has a fixed value?!
phrases.notes: An אשם must be worth at least two silver shekels (ויקרא 5:15).

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא מִפַּרְזִקְיָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי: וְלִפְרוֹךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the הצד השוה built in step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The הצד השוה argument from the עולה and bird חטאת, and with it אביי's claim in step 19.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both sources share a feature (no fixed value) that the אשם lacks, so their blood rule may not carry over to the אשם.

steps.title: A new reason: the word 'it' keeps blood-above for the חטאת alone
steps.stepSummary: Since the הצד השוה could be broken, the גמרא gives a different reason. The פסוק says 'the כהן who offers it', and 'it' teaches that only the חטאת's blood goes above, not the blood of any other offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is רבי אליעזר's reason: the פסוק says 'The כהן who offers it.' Its blood goes above, but the blood of another offering does not go above.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the logical proofs and gives רבי אליעזר's real reason: a word in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 19–24 tried to prove from logic that an אשם's blood goes below, and every proof was broken. Now the reason comes from the פסוק itself: 'אותה' (it) limits blood-above to the חטאת. So even though רבי אליעזר compares the אשם to the חטאת in other ways, the פסוק stops the comparison here.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; the earlier approach is dropped
This is the reason
Who offers it (as a חטאת)
Above the red line on the מזבח

steps.whyThisMatters: It shifts רבי אליעזר's position from a logical argument to a reading of the פסוק. The next steps test that reading.

phrases.english: Rather, this is the reason of רבי אליעזר:
As the verse says: 'The כהן who offers it'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:19

phrases.english: 'It': its blood goes above,
but the blood of another offering does not go above.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts that the הצד השוה in step 24 can be broken and replaces it with a reason from the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New source: a limiting word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אליעזר's view that an אשם's blood goes below rested on a הצד השוה, which step 24 showed could be broken.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word 'אותה' limits blood-above to the חטאת, so the אשם's blood goes below.

steps.title: Then 'it' should also limit the rule of לשמה to the חטאת
steps.stepSummary: If 'אותה' limits a rule to the חטאת, then the 'אותה' in the פסוק about slaughtering for its own sake should limit that rule too. Other offerings, the אשם included, would then stay valid even שלא לשמה, and רבי אליעזר says the opposite.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let him also say about the חטאת: 'it' teaches that a חטאת is valid when slaughtered for its own sake and invalid when not for its own sake. Then all other offerings are valid either way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the new reason by applying the same reading to a different 'אותה' in the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר holds that an אשם slaughtered שלא לשמה is invalid, just like a חטאת. But if 'אותה' always means 'only this one', the 'אותה' in the פסוק about slaughtering the חטאת for its own sake would leave every other offering valid. So רבי אליעזר does not seem to read 'אותה' consistently.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
For its own sake, with the correct intent for this offering
Not for its own sake, with the wrong intent
Other offerings

phrases.english: If so, let him also say about the חטאת:
'It': for its own sake it is valid,
phrases.notes: This is a different 'it': ויקרא 4:33, 'and slaughter it for a חטאת'.

phrases.english: not for its own sake it is invalid;
which would mean that other offerings,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין לִשְׁמָן בֵּין שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָן כְּשֵׁרִין!
phrases.english: whether for their own sake or not for their own sake, are valid!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of 'אותה' introduced in step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that 'אותה' limits a rule to the חטאת alone
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Read the same way, the 'אותה' about לשמה would leave an אשם valid שלא לשמה, which goes against רבי אליעזר's own ruling.

steps.title: The 'it' about לשמה is not exclusive, because of the פסח
steps.stepSummary: The 'אותה' about לשמה does not mean 'only the חטאת', since the פסח also has to be slaughtered for its own sake. That 'אותה' therefore cannot be limiting.
steps.simpleTranslation: That 'it' is not exact, because it left out the פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this particular 'אותה' cannot be limiting, because we know of another offering that follows the same rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We know the פסח is invalid שלא לשמה. If 'אותה' really meant 'only the חטאת', the פסח would be an exception to it. So that 'אותה' is not exclusive, and the אשם can be compared to the חטאת for לשמה.

keyTerms.meaning: Not exact; not meant to exclude everything else
Left out; there is another case the word does not cover
The קרבן פסח

phrases.english: That 'it' is not exact,
since it left out the פסח.
phrases.notes: Literally 'it left over'. The פסח also needs לשמה, so 'it' cannot mean 'only the חטאת'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 26 by showing that the 'אותה' about לשמה is not exclusive.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every 'אותה' limits its rule to the חטאת.
steps.terutzMaskana: The 'אותה' about לשמה is not limiting, because the פסח shares the rule.

steps.title: By that logic, the 'it' about blood above is not exclusive either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns the answer around. The bird עולה also has its blood above, so the 'אותה' about blood above also leaves out a case and should not be limiting. Then step 25's reason falls apart.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too it is not exact, because it left out the bird עולה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the answer from step 27 against step 25. Steps 29 and 30 answer this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 27 said that an 'אותה' which leaves out another case is not exclusive. The blood of a bird עולה also goes above, so the 'אותה' about blood above leaves out a case too. It should not be limiting, and then nothing stops the אשם's blood from going above like the חטאת's.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too
A bird brought as an עולה; its blood goes above the red line

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the bird עולה, whose blood goes above, with the bird חטאת from steps 21–23, whose blood goes below.

phrases.english: Here too, it is not exact,
since it left out the bird עולה!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the reasoning of step 27 to undo the source given in step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 25's claim that 'אותה' limits blood-above to the חטאת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If an 'אותה' that leaves out a case is not exclusive, the bird עולה shows that this 'אותה' is not exclusive either, so the אשם could have its blood above.

steps.title: Among slaughtered offerings, nothing is left out
steps.stepSummary: The 'אותה' about blood above still limits, because among slaughtered animals no other offering has its blood above. The bird עולה is not slaughtered at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: With regard to offerings that are slaughtered, at least, the תורה left nothing out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 28. The bird עולה does not count, because the פסוק is talking about slaughtered offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'אותה' about לשמה could not be limiting, because the פסח is a slaughtered animal and it was left out. The bird עולה is killed by מליקה, not by שחיטה, so it is outside the group the פסוק is talking about. Among slaughtered animals only the חטאת has blood above, so here 'אותה' really does limit, and step 25's reason stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Slaughtering an animal offering
At least, in any event
Left out, left over
Killing a bird offering by pinching the back of its neck (not slaughtering)

phrases.english: With regard to slaughtering, at least,
it did not leave out anything.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 28 and defends the reason given in step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the group the פסוק is talking about to slaughtered offerings
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bird עולה is also an offering with blood above, so 'אותה' leaves it out and cannot be limiting.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק only deals with slaughtered offerings. Among them, only the חטאת has blood above, so 'אותה' does limit.

steps.title: A second answer: the bird עולה's blood goes in a different place
steps.stepSummary: A second answer follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, who holds that the place for the חטאת's blood and the place for the bird עולה's blood are two different places.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you want, say: whose view is this? It is רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, who said: this place is one thing, and that place is another thing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another answer to step 28. The bird עולה's blood is not really put in the same place as the חטאת's blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the two offerings have different places for their blood, then the bird עולה is not a true example of 'the חטאת's kind of blood above'. So 'אותה' still leaves nothing out and can limit the rule to the חטאת. The next step brings the source showing that רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון holds this.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say (introduces another answer)
Whose opinion is this?
Separate, on its own

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
Whose view is this?
It is Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon,
who said: this place is separate,
phrases.notes: 'This place' is where the חטאת's blood goes, and 'that place' is where the bird עולה's blood goes.

phrases.english: and that place is separate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, separate answer to the challenge of step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the cases are different: the two offerings have different places for their blood
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bird עולה's blood is above just like the חטאת's, so 'אותה' leaves it out.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, the places are different, so the bird עולה is not left out and 'אותה' still limits.

steps.title: The ברייתא about the red line on the מזבח
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that blood for the lower part of the מזבח goes below the red line, and blood for the upper part goes above it. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says this is only for the bird עולה, while the animal חטאת's blood must go on the actual corner.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught in a ברייתא: The lower blood is placed from the red line and down, and the upper blood from the red line and up. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון said: When is this true? For a bird עולה. But for an animal חטאת, its blood is placed only on the corner itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון really holds that the two places are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Anywhere above the red line is fine for the bird עולה. The animal חטאת's blood must go exactly on the קרן, the corner of the מזבח. So the bird עולה's blood is 'above' in a different way, and step 30's answer is supported.

keyTerms.meaning: The red line around the middle of the מזבח, dividing its upper and lower halves
Blood that is placed on the lower half of the מזבח
A bird brought as an עולה
A corner of the מזבח
In what case are these words said? (limits an earlier rule)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers to the bird עולה problem. (1) The פסוק only deals with slaughtered offerings. (2) According to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, the bird עולה's blood goes anywhere above the red line, while the חטאת's blood goes on the corner itself. Either way, 'אותה' limits 'blood above' to the חטאת.

phrases.english: As it is taught: the lower blood
is placed from the red line and below,
and the upper blood from the red line and above.
Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon said:
In what case are these words said?
With a bird burnt offering;
but with an animal sin offering,
it itself is not done
except on the actual corner itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source for the view of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון that step 30 relied on.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון holds the bird עולה's blood and the חטאת's blood go in different places
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about the red line, where רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון limits 'anywhere above the line' to the bird עולה and requires the corner itself for the animal חטאת

steps.title: The משנה about blood brought into the היכל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה from elsewhere. רבי עקיבא says any blood brought into the היכל to atone becomes unfit. The חכמים say only a חטאת's blood. רבי אליעזר adds the אשם, based on 'כחטאת כאשם'.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: רבי עקיבא used to say that any blood that entered the היכל to atone is unfit. The חכמים say: only a חטאת. רבי אליעזר says: the אשם too, because the פסוק says 'as the חטאת, so the אשם'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new section by quoting a משנה with three opinions. It is setting up a discussion of these opinions that will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some blood is supposed to be put on the outside מזבח. If that blood was brought into the היכל instead, this משנה asks whether it becomes unfit. רבי עקיבא says it does for every offering, and the חכמים say only for a חטאת. רבי אליעזר again treats the אשם like a חטאת because of the פסוק 'כחטאת כאשם', just as he did with blood above in the earlier steps.

keyTerms.meaning: The inner building of the בית המקדש, inside, as opposed to the outside מזבח
Unfit, cannot be used
'As is the חטאת, so is the אשם' (ויקרא 7:7)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with blood that is supposed to go inside the היכל. This משנה is about blood meant for the outside מזבח that was wrongly brought inside.

phrases.english: We learned there:
phrases.notes: This משנה comes later in this מסכת, on דף 81b.

phrases.english: that Rabbi Akiva would say:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל דָּמִים שֶׁנִּכְנְסוּ לַהֵיכָל לְכַפֵּר – פְּסוּלִים.
phrases.english: Any blood that entered the Sanctuary to atone is unfit.
phrases.notes: He means blood that should have gone on the outside מזבח but was brought inside instead.

phrases.english: And the Sages say: only a sin offering.
Rabbi Eliezer says: also the guilt offering,
as it is said: 'As is the sin offering, so is the guilt offering.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:7

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן הָתָם, שֶׁהָיָה רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section with a משנה from elsewhere, again about רבי אליעזר treating the אשם like the חטאת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood brought into the היכל becomes unfit: for every offering according to רבי עקיבא, only for a חטאת according to the חכמים, and for a חטאת and an אשם according to רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: What is the reason of the חכמים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts רבי אליעזר's view, since he gave a source, and asks why the חכמים limit the rule to a חטאת alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: We understand רבי אליעזר, because he told us his reason. But what is the reason of the חכמים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the חכמים say only a חטאת becomes unfit when its blood is brought inside, and not an אשם. This question sets up רבא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר learned the אשם from the words 'כחטאת כאשם', which compare the two offerings. The חכמים did not explain why they reject that comparison. So the גמרא wants to know what keeps the אשם out of the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted; we understand this part (said before asking about the part we don't understand)
Reason or source
The חכמים, the majority opinion
What is the reason?

phrases.english: Granted, Rabbi Eliezer's view makes sense
since he states his reason
phrases.notes: His reason is the words 'כחטאת כאשם' from step 32, which put the אשם together with the חטאת.

phrases.english: but the Rabbis, what is their reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר כִּדְקָאָמַר טַעְמָא, אֶלָּא רַבָּנַן מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind the חכמים's position in the משנה quoted in step 32.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the חכמים leave the אשם out of the rule that blood brought into the היכל becomes unfit, even though 'כחטאת כאשם' seems to compare the two.

steps.title: רבא: a קל וחומר from the עולה blocks it
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that you cannot say an אשם whose blood went inside is unfit, because a קל וחומר from the עולה prevents it. The argument begins with 'just as' and continues in the next section.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: You cannot say that an אשם whose blood was brought inside is unfit, because of a קל וחומר from the עולה. Just as...
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the reason of the חכמים. A קל וחומר from the עולה means the אשם cannot be made unfit when its blood is brought inside. The text ends right as he starts laying out that קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does not attack the פסוק directly. He says logic blocks the idea: the עולה gives us a קל וחומר that does not fit with calling the אשם unfit. The details of how the קל וחומר works start with the word 'מה' and are spelled out in the next part of the גמרא.

keyTerms.meaning: A guilt offering
Inside, into the היכל
Unfit for the מזבח
You cannot say
A logical argument from a lighter case to a stricter one
A burnt offering

steps.confusionAlert: Don't stop at 'מה'. The sentence is not finished. The full קל וחומר from the עולה comes next.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: אָשָׁם נִכְנַס דָּמוֹ לִפְנִים פָּסוּל
phrases.english: Rava said: That a guilt offering whose blood entered inside is disqualified
phrases.notes: The Aramaic puts the idea first and 'you cannot say' after it. In plain English: you cannot say this אשם is unfit.

phrases.english: you cannot say,
because of an a fortiori argument from a burnt offering: Just as

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אָשָׁם נִכְנַס דָּמוֹ לִפְנִים פָּסוּל לָא מָצֵית אָמְרַתְּ, קַל וָחוֹמֶר מֵעוֹלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 33's question by giving the reasoning behind the חכמים's view.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The חכמים hold that an אשם whose blood was brought inside cannot be called unfit, because a קל וחומר from the עולה stands against it. The details of the קל וחומר continue in the next section.
